texture.memory.source: RGBA32 4 B/px; full mip chain approx base x 4/3 (Real-Time Rendering, mipmap memory overhead). 1536x1536x4=9437184; x4/3=12582912 (exact, no rounding needed for this dimension).
RGBA32 4 B/px x 4 textures, no mipmaps. Edge case: count > 1 must scale totalBytes linearly.
Microsoft DXGI BC7: 16 bytes per 4x4 block. blocks=(512/4)^2=16384; x16=262144.
EDGE CASE (non-power-of-two, non-block-multiple dimensions). BC7 blocks are always 4x4; ceil(1002/4)=251 blocks/axis; 251^2x16=1008016 (Microsoft DXGI BC7 spec).
Khronos ASTC spec: fixed 16 bytes/block regardless of block footprint; a 4x4 block therefore has the same bytes/pixel as BC7. 192^2x16=589824; x4/3=786432.

EDGE CASE: 1024 is not a multiple of 6. Khronos ASTC spec: 16 bytes/block, block=6x6 texels. ceil(1024/6)=171 blocks/axis; 171^2x16=467856. NOTE: the contract example in definicion-inicial.md Sec.9 (2048x2048 ASTC_6x6 -> 3355443 bytes) does not match this spec-based formula (it implies ~0.8 B/px instead of the correct 16/36=0.444 B/px); that example appears to be an AI-generated placeholder and must not be used as a reference value.
EDGE CASE: 1001 is not a multiple of 8. Khronos ASTC spec: 16 bytes/block, block=8x8 texels. ceil(1001/8)=126 blocks/axis; 126^2x16=254016.

texture.compare.source: Per-format block math per Khronos ASTC spec + Microsoft DXGI BC7 spec. EDGE CASE: 1024 is not a multiple of 6, so only ASTC_6x6 needs padding to 1026x1026; the other formats align exactly.

ASTC_6x6.note: mip factor 4/3 does not divide evenly here: 262144x4/3=349525.33 -> floor to nearest byte

texture.compare.source: 768 is exactly divisible by 4, 6 and 8 (no padding in any format), isolating the mip-chain x4/3 factor. EDGE CASE: ASTC_6x6 is the one format in this case where the x4/3 factor does not divide evenly -> defines the floor-to-nearest-byte rounding rule for mipmap totals.

count=2 scales totalBytes linearly for every format. EDGE CASE: 2048 is a multiple of 4 and 8 but not of 6 (ceil(2048/6)=342 blocks/axis, padded to 2052), exercising the ASTC_6x6 padding path at a different dimension than the other cases.

uv.texelDensity.source: density(px/m) = resolution / objectSize = 1024/2 = 512. 1 inch = 0.0254 m exactly (international yard/pound agreement, 1959); density(px/inch) = 512 x 0.0254 = 13.0048 (exact terminating decimal).

EDGE CASE: resolution must round to nearest power of two. desired = targetDensity x objectSize = 400; nearest power of two between 256 and 512: |400-256|=144 > |400-512|=112, so 512 wins. resulting density = 512/4 = 128 px/m.
EDGE CASE: inch unit, chosen so the 0.0254 m/inch conversion (exact by definition) lands on a whole number: 254 px/inch / 0.0254 m/inch = 10000 px/m exactly.

shader.math.source: EDGE CASE: t outside [0,1]. HLSL/GLSL lerp does not clamp t; it extrapolates linearly beyond [a,b]. -5 + 10*1.5 = 10.
EDGE CASE: value outside [inMin,inMax]. remap does not clamp by default, so the result extrapolates outside [outMin,outMax]. (15-0)/10*100=150.
smoothstep(e0,e1,x): t=clamp((x-e0)/(e1-e0),0,1); return t^2*(3-2t) (Khronos GLSL spec / HLSL smoothstep). t=0.5 -> 0.25*2=0.5.
EDGE CASE: x below edge0 clamps t to 0 per GLSL/HLSL spec, so the result is 0 regardless of how far below x is.
EDGE CASE: x above edge1 clamps t to 1 per GLSL/HLSL spec, so the result is 1 regardless of how far above x is.

color.convert.source: Standard RGB<->HSL conversion (CSS Color Module Level 3, section 7.2).
IEC 61966-2-1 sRGB transfer function: srgb = 1.055 * linear^(1/2.4) - 0.055 for linear > 0.0031308. Tolerance allowed per shared-tests/README.md (curve involves a non-terminating power).

EDGE CASE: exactly at the IEC 61966-2-1 breakpoint. At/below linear=0.0031308 the linear segment applies: srgb = linear * 12.92 (exact multiplication, no tolerance needed). 0.0031308*12.92=0.040449936.

EDGE CASE: exactly at the IEC 61966-2-1 breakpoint from the sRGB side. At/below srgb=0.04045 the linear segment applies: linear = srgb / 12.92 = 0.04045/12.92 = 0.0031308 (matches the linear-side breakpoint to the precision published in the standard, confirming both constants are consistent).
